## Definitions

- [statement] OSHA says engineering and work-practice controls should be the primary feasible means of reducing toxic chemical exposure; NIOSH describes source-capture ventilation for volatile printing-press emissions. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://www.osha.gov/chemical-hazards/ · keywords: Game product safety labeling and workshop hazards · also: https://www.cdc.gov/niosh/engcontrols/ecd/detail37.html

## Structure and components

- [statement] CPSC’s small-parts ban covers products intended for children under three, but exempts books and other articles made of paper; entirely paper pieces detached during use-and-abuse testing are also excluded from the small-part test. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://www.cpsc.gov/FAQ/Small-Parts-and-Choking-Hazard-Labeling-FAQs · keywords: Game product safety labeling and workshop hazards · also: https://www.cpsc.gov/Business--Manufacturing/Business-Education/Business-Guidance/Small-Parts-for-Toys-and-Childrens-Products
- [statement] CPSC permits reliance on component-supplier lead-test evidence only with due care and access to underlying test documentation, including valid testing by a CPSC-accepted laboratory. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://www.cpsc.gov/FAQ/Total-Lead-Content · keywords: Game product safety labeling and workshop hazards
- [statement] Reliance on a component supplier’s lead test or certificate requires due care and access to underlying test documentation; a bare supplier assurance is insufficient under CPSC’s explanation. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://www.cpsc.gov/FAQ/Total-Lead-Content · keywords: Game product safety labeling and workshop hazards

## How it works

- [statement] OSHA’s printing-press roll-cleaning case rejects the minor-servicing exception when workers bypass guards and lack effective alternative protection, even when cleaning is routine, repetitive and integral to production. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://www.osha.gov/etools/lockout-tagout/case-studies/printing-press-roll-cleaning · keywords: Game product safety labeling and workshop hazards

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] Small-parts warning requirements depend on the product and intended age, including applicable products for ages 3–6; advertising for toys subject to the warning must carry it too. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://www.cpsc.gov/Business--Manufacturing/Business-Education/Business-Guidance/CPSC-Labeling-Requirements-Overview · keywords: Game product safety labeling and workshop hazards · also: https://www.cpsc.gov/Business--Manufacturing/Business-Education/Business-Guidance/Small-Parts-for-Toys-and-Childrens-Products
- [statement] CPSC says paper and ordinary CMYK process printing inks can avoid third-party lead testing under material determinations; this does not remove the lead-content limit or the obligation to certify compliance. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://www.cpsc.gov/FAQ/Total-Lead-Content · keywords: Game product safety labeling and workshop hazards · also: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-16/chapter-II/subchapter-C/part-1500/section-1500.91
- [statement] The CMYK lead determination excludes spot colors, non-CMYK inks, inks outside the substrate and specified after-treatment printing; it cannot be extended automatically to every printed finish. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-04) — https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-16/chapter-II/subchapter-C/part-1500/section-1500.91 · keywords: Game product safety labeling and workshop hazards
- [statement] CPSC identifies specific choking-warning labeling rules for products containing small parts and intended for children between three and six; that scope should be checked separately from paper exemptions to the under-three small-parts ban. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://www.cpsc.gov/Business--Manufacturing/Business-Education/Business-Guidance/CPSC-Labeling-Requirements-Overview · keywords: Game product safety labeling and workshop hazards · also: https://www.cpsc.gov/FAQ/Small-Parts-and-Choking-Hazard-Labeling-FAQs
- [statement] CPSC says accessible children’s-product components must meet a total lead limit of 100 ppm and paint or similar surface coatings a separate 90 ppm limit. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://www.cpsc.gov/FAQ/Total-Lead-Content · keywords: Game product safety labeling and workshop hazards

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] OSHA requires guarding where operation exposes employees to injury and lists guillotine cutters; the guard must prevent access to the danger zone during the operating cycle, rather than merely warn. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://www.osha.gov/laws-regs/regulations/standardnumber/1910/1910.212 · keywords: Game product safety labeling and workshop hazards · also: https://www.osha.gov/laws-regs/standardinterpretations/2004-04-07
- [statement] UK HSE identifies failure to refit guards as a major cause of printing-industry accidents. This supports guard-restoration checks as an operational concern, rather than establishing a US legal requirement. (low confidence) — https://www.hse.gov.uk/printing/faqs.htm · keywords: Game product safety labeling and workshop hazards
- [statement] OSHA lists guillotine cutters among machines usually requiring point-of-operation guarding; hand tools for placing or removing material supplement rather than replace required guards. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://www.osha.gov/etools/machine-guarding/introduction/general-requirements · keywords: Game product safety labeling and workshop hazards

## Facts and statements

- [statement] CPSC classifies a children’s product by primary intended use for children aged 12 or younger, considering reasonable manufacturer statements, marketing, consumer recognition and age-determination guidance; an age label alone does not control classification. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://www.cpsc.gov/FAQ/Childrens-Products · keywords: Game product safety labeling and workshop hazards
- [statement] CPSC treats traditional playing cards and similar games appealing to a general audience as general-use products; child-oriented features or junior packaging can change that classification. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://www.cpsc.gov/FAQ/Childrens-Products · keywords: Game product safety labeling and workshop hazards
- [statement] For toys primarily intended for children aged 12 or younger, CPSC requires applicable third-party testing by an accepted laboratory and a Children’s Product Certificate; the manufacturer or importer must identify applicable toy-standard sections. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://www.cpsc.gov/FAQ/Toy-Safety · keywords: Game product safety labeling and workshop hazards · also: https://www.cpsc.gov/FAQ/Childrens-Products
- [statement] CPSC distinguishes ASTM F963’s under-14 toy scope from the federal third-party-testing threshold for products intended primarily for children 12 or younger. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://www.cpsc.gov/FAQ/Toy-Safety · keywords: Game product safety labeling and workshop hazards
- [statement] CPSC exempts labeling, instructions and producer markings from third-party laboratory testing, while requiring CPC certification of all applicable toy-standard sections. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://www.cpsc.gov/FAQ/Toy-Safety · keywords: Game product safety labeling and workshop hazards
- [statement] Children’s products need permanent tracking information on product and packaging to the extent practicable, including the responsible firm, production date and location, and identifying production information such as a batch or run number. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://www.cpsc.gov/FAQ/Tracking-Label · keywords: Game product safety labeling and workshop hazards · also: https://www.cpsc.gov/Business--Manufacturing/Business-Education/Business-Guidance/CPSC-Labeling-Requirements-Overview, https://www.cpsc.gov/FAQ/Toy-Safety
- [statement] CPSC distinguishes a toy’s substantive flammability obligations from premarket testing: the FHSA prohibits hazardous flammable children’s toys even though this requirement does not mandate premarket or third-party testing. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://www.cpsc.gov/FAQ/Toy-Safety · keywords: Game product safety labeling and workshop hazards
- [statement] OSHA’s printing interpretation limits the minor-servicing exception to routine, repetitive, integral production work with effective alternative protection. Normal guillotine blade changing requires an energy-control procedure with lockout/tagout and any necessary guarding. (low confidence) (verified as of 2004-04-07) — https://www.osha.gov/laws-regs/standardinterpretations/2004-04-07 · keywords: Game product safety labeling and workshop hazards
- [statement] The MBM-hosted manual describes a movable guard and two-hand control as cutting safeguards for IDEAL 6655. (low confidence) — https://mbmcorp.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/09/TRIUMPH-6655-op-manual-1399.pdf · keywords: Game product safety labeling and workshop hazards
- [statement] Where OSHA’s Hazard Communication standard applies, employers need a written program for chemical labels, SDSs and training; SDSs must be immediately accessible, and training covers initial assignment and new chemical hazards. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://www.osha.gov/laws-regs/regulations/standardnumber/1910/1910.1200 · keywords: Game product safety labeling and workshop hazards
- [statement] NIOSH identifies inhalation and skin-contact hazards during press cleaning. Its printing LEV example reports vapor and dust measurement reductions of 83 percent and 67 percent; these are case results, not workshop performance predictions. (low confidence) — https://www.cdc.gov/niosh/engcontrols/ecd/detail37.html · keywords: Game product safety labeling and workshop hazards
- [statement] A NIOSH educational vignette links visual symptoms to an amine-containing additive used with water-based ink. NIOSH calls the story loosely based on evaluations and cautions that its facility-specific recommendations may not generalize. (low confidence) — https://www.cdc.gov/niosh/bulletin/2015/medical-mystery1b.html · keywords: Game product safety labeling and workshop hazards
- [statement] OSHA’s lithography guidance identifies repeated reaching, pinching, prolonged standing and low-table bending in hand collation; it recommends reachable stacks, adjusted work height, posture variation and reduced exposure time. (low confidence) — https://www.osha.gov/etools/printing-industry/lithography · keywords: Game product safety labeling and workshop hazards
- [statement] CPSC’s labeling overview still names ASTM F963-17, whereas its Toy Safety FAQ names ASTM F963-23 with an April 20, 2024 effective date. This is a mismatch between the two cited pages, not evidence that both editions currently govern. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://www.cpsc.gov/Business--Manufacturing/Business-Education/Business-Guidance/CPSC-Labeling-Requirements-Overview · keywords: Game product safety labeling and workshop hazards · also: https://www.cpsc.gov/FAQ/Toy-Safety
- [statement] CPSC allows a reusable storage container to satisfy on-product marking for some multi-piece children’s products; it also says there is no tracking-label exemption based on business size. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://www.cpsc.gov/FAQ/Tracking-Label · keywords: Game product safety labeling and workshop hazards
- [statement] NIOSH identifies press-cleaning solvent vapors and skin absorption as printing hazards; its control guidance describes local exhaust that captures vapor near the press and exhausts it outside with replacement air. (low confidence) — https://www.cdc.gov/niosh/engcontrols/ecd/detail37.html · keywords: Game product safety labeling and workshop hazards
- [statement] In the printing study summarized by NIOSH, local exhaust reduced measured real-time vapor by 83 percent and dust by 67 percent; these are study results, not a guaranteed reduction for another workshop. (low confidence) — https://www.cdc.gov/niosh/engcontrols/ecd/detail37.html · keywords: Game product safety labeling and workshop hazards
- [statement] For employers using hazardous workplace chemicals, OSHA requires labels, safety data sheets and worker training about hazards and protective measures. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://www.osha.gov/chemical-hazards/ · keywords: Game product safety labeling and workshop hazards
- [statement] OSHA’s lithography guidance identifies repetitive forceful paper gripping, awkward wrist postures and bending in finishing work; suggested controls include smaller handled stacks, neutral hand postures and adjustable work surfaces. (low confidence) — https://www.osha.gov/etools/printing-industry/lithography · keywords: Game product safety labeling and workshop hazards
